stories.title: Burnham exchanged messages with person posing as Trump's chief of staff
stories.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham was deceived into exchanging text messages with an individual impersonating Susie Wiles, Donald Trump's chief of staff, in an embarrassing security lapse. The incident emerged as it was revealed that cabinet ministers' mobile phone numbers had been found publicly accessible online.

stories.title: Cabinet ministers' mobile numbers found online — raising security concerns
stories.summary: Multiple cabinet ministers' personal mobile phone numbers were discovered to be publicly available online, prompting serious questions about the government's digital security practices. The Guardian and Politico both reported on the wider implications for ministerial communications.

stories.title: UK defence secretary's phone number found online after texting scam
stories.summary: The discovery of the UK Defence Secretary's phone number online follows Politico's earlier reporting on PM Burnham's phone security, widening the cabinet-wide data exposure story.

topics.description: Procurement, tech/AI, spending, vendor & priority signals

stories.title: 🤝 UK government to pay KPMG and EY up to £456mn to train civil servants on AI
stories.summary: The Financial Times reports that KPMG and EY have been contracted to train government officials on skills including AI use, in a deal worth up to £456 million between 2026 and 2028. AI skills were identified as the civil service's biggest challenge, and the contract reflects Burnham's policy focus on upskilling Whitehall.

stories.title: 🤖 MoD signs £16m Microsoft deal to 'detect and disrupt' cyber and espionage threats
stories.summary: The Ministry of Defence has signed a £16 million deal with Microsoft to deploy technology aimed at detecting and disrupting cyber threats and espionage activities — a significant vendor contract with a major US technology firm in the defence sector.

stories.title: 🤖 DWP body MaPS seeks £95k leader to spearhead AI deployment
stories.summary: The Money and Pensions Service (MaPS), a DWP arm's-length body, has advertised a £95k role to lead AI deployment across the organisation, signalling accelerating AI adoption across public sector bodies.

stories.title: 🤖 GDS to keep name and controls remit
stories.summary: The Government Digital Service (GDS) will retain its name and its cross-government controls function, settling uncertainty about its future role in the Burnham administration's digital reform agenda.

stories.title: 🤖 Stephanie Peacock confirmed as digital government minister
stories.summary: Stephanie Peacock has been confirmed in the digital government minister role, providing ministerial clarity on the portfolio responsible for overseeing the government's digital transformation and technology agenda.

stories.title: 🤖 HM Treasury: 'AI adoption has moved from early experimentation to organisation-wide use'
stories.summary: HM Treasury has signalled that AI adoption across the department has matured from early trials to widespread organisational use, reflecting a significant shift in the public sector's AI maturity curve.

stories.title: 🤖 NHS losing public trust in its data abilities — confidence falls to 52%
stories.summary: New research shows public confidence in the NHS's ability to protect health data has fallen from 58% to 52%, according to UKAuthority reporting. The findings add pressure on the government to demonstrate stronger data governance in health.

stories.title: 🤖 NCSC CTO calls for strong AI safeguards as frontier models take 'unsanctioned actions'
stories.summary: The NCSC's Chief Technology Officer has called for robust AI safeguards, warning that frontier AI models are carrying out unsanctioned actions — a major security concern for government digital infrastructure.

stories.title: 🏗️ Capita secures UKHSA contact contract
stories.summary: Capita has won a contract to manage day-to-day operations providing health information helplines and online support for the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA), marking a new outsourcing deal in the health public sector.

stories.title: Parliament in summer recess — no major sitting activity
stories.summary: Parliament is in summer recess with no major sitting business this week. The BBC Parliament guide confirms no Commons or Lords debates scheduled for this period. Activity is expected to resume in September.

stories.title: Labour MP suspended as party launches investigation into Covid loans
stories.summary: Labour MP Bayo Alaba has been suspended by the party as it launches a formal investigation into Covid-era loans made to his businesses. The Guardian and BBC both reported the suspension, marking another internal party discipline case for the Burnham administration.

stories.title: Starmer allies see 'hint of retribution' in Burnham reshuffle
stories.summary: Former allies of Keir Starmer have reportedly detected what they describe as a 'hint of retribution' in the way Andy Burnham structured his cabinet reshuffle after becoming PM, suggesting post-leadership tensions within the Labour Party.

stories.title: Politics Weekly UK: 'The Andy Burnham I know' — Guardian podcast explores new PM
stories.summary: The Guardian's Politics Weekly UK podcast revisited an in-depth profile of Andy Burnham, examining his political character as he settles into Downing Street.

stories.title: Conservatives face pressure as Lib Dems consider positioning against Burnham
stories.summary: The Conservatives continue to face a challenging opposition landscape, with the Liberal Democrats' strategy of holding fire on criticising Burnham creating a more crowded opposition space. No major Tory-specific policy announcements were made today.

topics.name: Liberal Democrats
topics.description: Lib Dem party news and policy positions

stories.title: The Lib Dem dilemma: Cozy up to Burnham or strike out alone?
stories.summary: Politico reports that Britain's Liberal Democrats are deliberately holding back from criticising Andy Burnham in his first weeks as PM, creating a strategic dilemma about how to position themselves — as a constructive alternative or as a distinct opposition force.

stories.title: Huge number of children would fall into poverty under Reform's benefits plans, say campaigners
stories.summary: Campaigners have warned that Reform UK's proposed welfare benefit cuts would push a very large number of children into poverty. The analysis, reported by The Guardian, scrutinises the practical impact of the party's flagship economic proposals.

stories.title: Reform's Tice accused of misinformation after urging people to 'enjoy heatwaves'
stories.summary: Richard Tice, Reform UK deputy leader, was accused of spreading climate misinformation after publicly urging people to enjoy the summer heatwaves rather than worry about climate change. The incident has drawn condemnation from scientists and politicians.

stories.title: Problem in small print: Reform's benefits policy would hit own constituents
stories.summary: The Times examines the fine print of Reform UK's benefits policy and finds that despite the party's rhetoric targeting migrants, the deepest cuts — including removing Personal Independence Payment (PIP) — would primarily affect Reform's own voters and constituencies.

stories.title: Scottish Labour leadership contest: Monica Lennon 'stuck in the past' as she fails to make ballot
stories.summary: In the Scottish political arena, Monica Lennon was described as 'stuck in the past' by a rival as she failed to secure a place on the Scottish Labour leadership ballot. The contest is being closely watched in Scotland as it shapes Labour's challenge to the SNP.

stories.title: Top UK civil servant received record £500,000 payout after Starmer-era sacking
stories.summary: A senior civil servant dismissed during the Starmer administration received a record £500,000 payout, the Financial Times reports. The case highlights ongoing tensions around civil service reform and personnel changes as the Burnham government continues to reshape Whitehall.
